templates.basis: Verbatim example text published in FBI IC3 PSA240412; agency/amounts/URL are slots in the original pattern
templates.text: {AGENCY}: We've noticed an outstanding toll amount of ${AMT} on your record. To avoid a late fee of ${FEE}, visit {URL} to settle your balance.

templates.basis: Template of FTC Jan 2025 alert mechanics: text out of the blue, dollar amount owed, link to a page asking for bank/card info
templates.text: {AGENCY}: You have an unpaid toll of ${AMT}. Pay now to avoid additional late fees: {URL}

templates.basis: Template of FTC Jan 2025 alert mechanics: unpaid tolls, pay immediately, dollar amount, link
templates.text: Final notice: your vehicle has an outstanding toll balance of ${AMT}. If unpaid by {DATE}, a late fee of ${FEE} will be added. Pay here: {URL}

templates.basis: Template of FTC Jan 2025 alert mechanics: scammers pretend to be tolling agencies and demand money by text with a link
templates.text: {AGENCY} reminder: unpaid toll charges of ${AMT} were recorded for your vehicle. Settle your balance today at {URL} to keep your account in good standing.

templates.basis: Template built from the FTC Jul 2025 alert's own description: overdue traffic ticket, link to pay, threats to report to the 'DMV violation database', suspend registration/license/driving privileges, additional 35% service fee
templates.text: {STATE} Department of Motor Vehicles Final Notice: Our records show you have an overdue traffic ticket. Pay by {DATE} or we will report you to the DMV violation database, suspend your vehicle registration, license, and driving privileges, and charge an additional 35% service fee. Pay now: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jul 2025 alert threats: suspension of driving privileges, prosecution, credit score damage
templates.text: {STATE} DMV: You have an outstanding traffic ticket of ${AMT}. Failure to pay by {DATE} may result in suspension of your driving privileges, prosecution, and damage to your credit score. Resolve here: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jul 2025 alert mechanics: unexpected text that looks like it is from the state DMV, overdue ticket, pay immediately or privileges suspended
templates.text: FINAL NOTICE - {STATE} DMV: An unpaid traffic violation remains on your record. Pay ${AMT} within 24 hours to avoid license suspension and additional fees: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jul 2025 alert mechanics: claim of an overdue traffic ticket with a link to pay and suspension warning
templates.text: {STATE} Department of Motor Vehicles: Our records indicate an overdue traffic citation. If not paid by {DATE}, your registration and license will be suspended. Pay online: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jan 2026 alert wording: message looks like it is from the IRS or a state tax office saying they have 'processed' or 'approved' your tax refund claim; click a link to verify identity
templates.text: IRS Notice: Your {YEAR} tax refund of ${AMT} has been approved. To claim your refund, verify your identity within 24 hours: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jan 2026 alert: to 'verify your identity' and 'send you money' they ask for Social Security and bank account numbers via a link
templates.text: {AGENCY_TAX}: We have processed your tax refund claim of ${AMT}. Confirm your Social Security number and bank account details to receive your payment: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from IRS Dirty Dozen 2026 item 1: texts that appear to be from the IRS direct taxpayers to fake IRS websites to claim refunds
templates.text: Your federal tax refund of ${AMT} is ready. Complete verification now to avoid delays: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jan 2026 alert: IRS or state tax office impersonation, refund approved, enter details at a link
templates.text: {STATE} Department of Revenue: Your state tax refund of ${AMT} has been approved. Verify your information here to release your refund: {URL}

templates.basis: Family variant specified for v4 (refund approved, quality inspection, no return needed) written as a template of the FTC Mar 2024 Amazon-impersonation pattern: it is not Amazon contacting you; the story ends with the victim sending money or account details
templates.text: Amazon: A refund of ${AMT} for your recent order has been approved. Due to a quality inspection issue, no return is needed. Confirm your payment details to receive your refund: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Mar 2024 alert: a call or text about a suspicious charge/purchase on your Amazon account that is not really Amazon
templates.text: Amazon alert: We detected a suspicious purchase of ${AMT} on your account. If you did not make this purchase, verify your account now: {URL}

templates.basis: Family variant specified for v4 (full refund, keep the item, no return required) in the FTC Mar 2024 Amazon-impersonation pattern
templates.text: Your Amazon order #{ORDER} qualifies for a full refund of ${AMT}. Keep the item - no return required. Claim your refund here: {URL}

templates.basis: Template of FTC Mar 2024 Amazon-impersonation pattern: fake Amazon contact about an account problem that pushes the victim to act and hand over details
templates.text: Amazon Customer Service: Your refund of ${AMT} is on hold. Verify your billing information within 24 hours to release it: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2025 task-scam alert: unexpected message offering 'work' doing 'optimization' or 'product boosting' online; FTC Apr 2026 alert: fake recruiters mention daily pay rates and ask you to reply YES or INTERESTED
templates.text: Hi! We are hiring for online product boosting tasks. Earn ${RATE}/day working from home, paid daily. Reply YES to get started.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2025 alert: to unlock the next set of tasks and get 'earnings' out, the scammer tells you to deposit your own money, usually in crypto
templates.text: You have earned ${AMT} in commissions. To unlock your next set of tasks and withdraw your earnings, deposit ${DEP} in crypto to activate your account.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2025 alert mechanics: fake earnings grow in the app, small early payouts of $5 to $20 build trust, then a deposit is demanded
templates.text: Congratulations, your balance is ${AMT}. Complete one VIP task set to withdraw. A refundable deposit of ${DEP} is required first.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2025 alert: task scams begin with an unexpected message on WhatsApp, Telegram, text, or social media offering quick money for tasks
templates.text: Work from home doing simple optimization tasks, ${RATE} per day, no experience needed. Message us on WhatsApp to begin: {PHONE}

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2025 alert: deposit your own money to unlock tasks and release earnings; the earnings are fake and the real money is gone
templates.text: Great job! Your earnings of ${AMT} are ready. Send a small deposit of ${DEP} to unlock the withdrawal of your full balance.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2024 alert: a text from a number you do not know asking when you are free to catch up over a cup of coffee
templates.text: Hi, is this {NAME}? Are we still on for coffee tomorrow?

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2024 alert title/premise: 'When are you free for coffee?' from a supposed long lost friend
templates.text: Hey {NAME}, when are you free for coffee? It has been too long, we should catch up!

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2024 alert: they apologize, keep the conversation going, then pitch a secret way to make big money using cryptocurrency
templates.text: Sorry, I think I have the wrong number. Anyway, you seem kind. Do you know anything about crypto investing? I made ${AMT} last month and can teach you my secret.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2024 alert mechanics: wrong-number reply confirms the number works, scammer apologizes and pitches a cryptocurrency scam
templates.text: Oops, wrong person! My apologies. You sound nice though - do you want to keep chatting? I can show you how I earn money with cryptocurrency.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Aug 2024 alert premise: friendly message from an unknown number addressed to someone else, designed to start a conversation
templates.text: Hi {NAME}, is the golf game still on for {DAY}? Let me know.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jun 2026 alert: missed jury duty, threat of arrest, pay a fine using a payment app or cryptocurrency; IC3 PSA260917 adds prepaid cards as a demanded payment method
templates.text: COURT NOTICE: You failed to appear for jury duty. A warrant has been issued for your arrest. Pay your fine of ${AMT} today using a payment app or gift cards to avoid arrest. Call {PHONE} now.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jun 2026 alert: caller claims to be a U.S. Marshal or local police officer, says you missed jury duty and threatens arrest unless you pay a fine
templates.text: This is the U.S. Marshals Service. Our records show you missed jury duty and a bench warrant is active in your name. Resolve your fine of ${AMT} immediately or you will be arrested.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jun 2026 alert twist: a text or email with a document that looks like an official warrant for your arrest, complete with how much you owe for missing jury duty
templates.text: URGENT: A warrant for your arrest has been issued for failure to appear for jury service. View your warrant and pay the ${AMT} fine here: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from IC3 PSA260917: scammer accuses the victim of missing a court date and says there is a warrant for their arrest unless a payment is made
templates.text: {COUNTY} Sheriff's Office: You have an outstanding warrant for missing a court date. Pay ${AMT} by phone today to clear the warrant and avoid arrest.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Oct 2026 alert script: a phone was registered under your name and is being used to commit scams in another country; the 'official' reads off a badge ID; if you do not cooperate they threaten to deactivate your phone number
templates.text: This is Agent {NAME} with the Federal Trade Commission, badge #{BADGE}. A phone registered in your name is being used to commit scams in another country. Your number will be deactivated within 24 hours unless you cooperate.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jun 2026 alert: they say they are an FTC employee or 'agent' who can help you 'recover losses' from a previous scam, and send a photo of an employee ID and badge to 'verify' their identity
templates.text: FTC: I am sending you a photo of my employee ID and badge to verify my identity. I can help you recover the money you lost. A processing fee is required to start your recovery.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Jun 2026 alert + FTC Refund and Recovery Scams article: recovery offered for an upfront fee ('processing fee'/'retainer fee'), or asked to move money into an account they specify
templates.text: Federal Trade Commission: We can recover the ${AMT} you lost in a scam. Pay the recovery fee first and move your money to the account we specify so we can protect it.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Oct 2026 alert: they tell you to keep everything secret; later they claim you are under arrest unless you send money for a security deposit; a real FTC employee will never threaten to disconnect your phone
templates.text: This is the FTC. Keep this conversation secret. Do not tell your bank or family. Send money for a security deposit today or your phone service will be disconnected.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Job Scams article fake-check mechanics: the employer sends a check, asks you to deposit it and send some money back; FTC Apr 2026 alert repeats the deposit-check-and-send-money-back pattern for equipment
templates.text: Congratulations, you are hired for the remote position! We are mailing you a check for ${AMT} to buy your equipment. Deposit the check and send the remaining balance to our equipment vendor.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Job Scams article: victims end up paying for starter kits, so-called training, or certifications that are useless
templates.text: Welcome aboard! Your starter kit and training materials cost ${AMT}. Pay today so we can ship your equipment and set your start date.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Job Scams article: deposit the check, keep part for your services, send the rest to someone else - the check is fake and bounces
templates.text: Your first paycheck check of ${AMT} has been issued for equipment purchases. Deposit it today and forward ${DEP} to the supplier we use.

templates.basis: Template from FTC Apr 2026 alert: they say they have a check you need to deposit and then ask you to send them money back
templates.text: HR: To complete onboarding, purchase your home office equipment using the check we sent, then send the overpayment back to us right away.

templates.basis: Template from IC3 PSA261015-3 Voter Registration Scheme: victims receive a text or email stating they are not registered to vote in their state and are encouraged to click a link to a fraudulent state voter registration page
templates.text: Our records show you are not registered to vote in {STATE}. Confirm your registration before the deadline or you will not be able to vote: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from IC3 PSA261015-3: 'not registered to vote in their state' message with a link to a fake registration page that steals PII
templates.text: {STATE} Elections: Your voter registration status is INACTIVE. Update your information here to restore your registration: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from IC3 PSA261015-3 voter registration scheme mechanics (text/email + link + fake state page)
templates.text: Voter alert: We could not verify your registration for the upcoming election. Check your status and re-register now: {URL}

templates.basis: Template from IC3 PSA261015-3: message states you are not registered to vote in your state and pushes a link before the election
templates.text: You are NOT registered to vote in {STATE}. Register before {DATE} to receive your ballot: {URL}

templates.basis: Template of the verification-code takeover pattern in FTC guidance: a scammer triggers a code to your phone, then contacts you asking you to hand it over (FTC Google Voice verification-code alert; FTC rule: anyone who asks you for your verification code is a scammer)
templates.text: Hi, I sent a 6-digit code to your number by mistake. Can you please send me the code? It is urgent.

templates.basis: Template of FTC verification-code guidance: scammers pretend to be someone you can trust, say there is a problem with your account, and ask for the verification code to get into it; FTC Jun 2026 alert notes fake FTC contact also arrives via WhatsApp
templates.text: Hello, this is WhatsApp support. Your account will be suspended. Share the verification code we just sent you to confirm your identity.

templates.basis: Template of the code-forwarding takeover: the 'sent it by mistake' pretext used to obtain a code the scammer triggered (FTC verification-code guidance pattern)
templates.text: Sorry, I accidentally sent my WhatsApp code to you. Please forward me the 6-digit code you received.

templates.basis: Template of FTC verification-code guidance pattern: a message asks the victim to reply with the code sent to their phone so the scammer can log in as them
templates.text: Your WhatsApp verification code is needed to complete your account verification. Reply with the code you received by text.

meta.purpose: Scam Shield v4 seed templates for the 2026 scam families. Seeds come ONLY from US-government publications (FTC consumer alerts/articles, FBI IC3 PSAs, IRS newsroom) fetched 2026-11-18, or are faithful templates of the exact script mechanics those publications describe. Slot placeholders like {AMT}, {URL}, {STATE} are filled ONLY by deterministic code in augment_v4.py (fixed lists, fictional 555 numbers, code-generated lookalike URLs). No LLM wrote any seed text; no social-media posts were used as data.
meta.split_rule: Per family, template index 1 is validation-only and index 3 is test-only; all other templates are train. The held-out 2026-family test therefore contains seed templates the model never trained on.
